why:
D16. Spring routes are read by `pkg/jvm_routes.py`, which the Kotlin and Java front-ends share: the *semantics* — verb mapping, class-prefix joining, the no-`ANY` rule — are identical in both languages, and only the grammar differs. This case pins the Kotlin half; `java/spring_routes` pins the Java half against the same rules.

**The class stereotype is load-bearing, not ceremony.** `TopicClient` carries `@GetMapping("/remote/topics")` on an interface with no `@Controller`/`@RestController`, and yields nothing. That is the exact shape of a Spring Cloud OpenFeign **client**: the same annotations declare a route a service *calls*. Reading it as an endpoint would make every consumer look like a provider and quietly corrupt `pkg joins`, which is the one thing endpoints exist for.

`@Controller` counts as well as `@RestController` — `@RestController` is just `@Controller` plus `@ResponseBody`, both register handler mappings, and the validation repository (spring-petclinic-kotlin) uses the plain one throughout. An earlier draft of D16 named only `@RestController` and would have found nothing there.

The other rules each get a method. `root` has a bare `@GetMapping`, so it serves the class prefix itself. `vets` writes `"vets.json"` with no leading slash, which Spring allows and the join normalises. `replace` names its verb through `method = [RequestMethod.PUT]`. `anything` has a verb-less `@RequestMapping` and yields **nothing** — the no-`ANY` rule: inventing an `ANY` verb would put a word in the graph that appears nowhere in the source, and expanding it to seven endpoints would invent six routes nobody wrote. `AdminController`'s prefix is a constant reference rather than a literal, so every method in it is silenced: a method path without its real prefix names a route that does not exist.

The file also exercises a grammar defence. tree-sitter-kotlin 1.1.0 parses a top-level annotation with parenthesised arguments as a standalone expression and strips the declaration's `modifiers` — so `@RestController @RequestMapping("/api") class TopicController` arrives with *no* annotations at all unless they are recovered from the stranded node. 24 files in the validation app and 8 in the Ktor sample corpus hit this; without the recovery in `kotlin_names.annotations_of` this case reads two of its four classes as plain classes.

false_positives.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. `TopicClient` is an interface with `@GetMapping` and no controller stereotype — the Spring Cloud OpenFeign shape, where those annotations declare a route the service *calls*. A reader that keys off the mapping annotation alone reports it as a provider, and `pkg joins` then pairs a consumer with itself. Requiring `@Controller`/`@RestController` on the class is what prevents it.

PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. A verb-less `@RequestMapping` matches every method, and there is no honest Endpoint for that. `ANY` is a verb no client can send and no other front-end emits, so it would never join to anything; expanding it into seven endpoints would invent six routes the source does not contain.

excluded: `AdminController.purge` yields NO endpoint: its class prefix is `@RequestMapping(ADMIN_PREFIX)`, a constant reference rather than a literal. The class and its members are still emitted — only the routes are withheld, because `/purge` without its real prefix is a path nothing serves.
`TopicController.helper` carries no mapping annotation and yields nothing, which is the ordinary case and is here to show the reader does not treat every method of a controller as a route.
`ADMIN_PREFIX` is a top-level property, deliberately not a Field (D6).

Annotations arriving via `org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*` produce no IMPORTS edge: a wildcard names no single symbol. Only the explicit `import org.springframework.stereotype.Controller` does, and its target is external so it stays out of the node ratio while the edge counts. This is how spring-petclinic-kotlin is actually written — the wildcard is why `resolves_into_spring` has to accept one.
open_questions: Should a `const val` class prefix resolve? `ADMIN_PREFIX` is a compile-time constant, and the Compose route reader (D14) already collects bare top-level `const val`s across a whole walk. Sharing that table with the Spring reader would turn this case's silenced class into `GET /admin/purge`. Deliberately not done in P6: the two readers would have to agree on a constant table that also handles qualified references, and a half-resolved prefix is exactly the failure the refusal prevents.
